newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK PBK TO SOON SIGN CONSERVATION CREDIT LINE.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK PBK TO SOON SIGN CONSERVATION CREDIT LINE.

text.p: Slovak Priemyselna Banka a.s. (PBK) said on Monday it would soon sign an 18.8 million ECU eight-year credit line with the EBRD and EU for energy conservation projects at small and medium-sized private firms.
"We won the economy ministry tender to manage this credit line and everything points to a signing in early December," Viera Dubikova, head of the forex trading department at PBK, told Reuters.

The facility, two-thirds financed by the EBRD while the remainder will be funded by the EU, is to finance energy-saving investments, eventually aimed at helping to improve Slovak industry's energetic inefficiency, Dubikova said.

She declined to provide terms of the line at this stage, but added: "We have already been choosing clients, and we will probably manage to extend loans to some 25-26 firms, presumably from early next year".
Last week, Jiri Huebner, head of EBRD's Czech and Slovak team, told Reuters part of the credit line would carry a zero interest rate, making the average interest rate "very competetive".

The essential criteria for the clients will be to use the funds for low-energy production lines or equipment, so that 40 percent of these investments is repaid in saved energy in less than four years.
